judgements.reason: Both completed roadmaps are fully present in the pinned Tau Ceti, IntegralLattice and FiniteBilinearModule through typeE₈IsometryD8Plus on one side and hermiteHilbertBasis, weightL2Isometry, prodHilbertBasis and chebyshevTHilbertBasis on the other. Neither needs any new theory (only optional extras such as a root-datum bridge or L² operator packaging remain), so they cannot be separated.

StablePeriodicCurved still needs Happel's triangulated stable category, Gorenstein-projectives with Buchweitz's D_sg equivalence, periodic derived categories with Stai's theorems, curved DG modules with Positselski's second-kind derived categories and matrix factorizations with Eisenbud and Orlov. OrthogonalL2Bases is entirely built in Tau Ceti (hermiteHilbertBasis, prodHilbertBasis, chebyshevTHilbertBasis).

Serre weights needs integral modular curves with moduli stacks and GAGA, Katz forms with Hasse and theta operators, Raynaud and Breuil–Kisin finite flat theory with p-adic period rings, and Deligne's Galois representations resting on Weil II and local Langlands for GL₂. StablePeriodicCurved is a large but self-contained homological-algebra development (Happel, Buchweitz, Positselski, Orlov) on Mathlib's triangulated categories and Tau Ceti's exact structures, morphism ideals and DG algebras.

ArithmeticStatistics must add binary-quartic and ring parametrizations, Davenport's lattice-point lemma, uniformity sieves, p-adic masses and class field theory for class-group moments, on top of Tau Ceti's 2-Selmer group and Mordell–Weil theorem. Serre weights instead needs whole unbuilt towers: integral modular curves and stacks, Katz forms and theta operators, finite flat group schemes with Breuil–Kisin modules and p-adic period rings, and étale-cohomological Galois representations of eigenforms with Weil II.

Tropical must first complete nonarchimedean analytic geometry (Tau Ceti adic-space layers 3–5, formal schemes and generic fibres, Berkovich spaces) and then build semistable reduction and intersection theory on models, skeleta, the tropicalization structure theorem, faithful tropicalization and Mumford uniformization, a taller stack than ArithmeticStatistics' parametrizations, Davenport lemma, geometric sieve, p-adic masses and class field theory. The p-adic Hodge chain recorded for ArithmeticStatistics (RP.1 → R02.6) is not used by the Bhargava–Shankar argument, so its larger recorded closure overstates it.

Both need the unbuilt adic-space and formal-model layers, but AdicEtaleGeometry adds perfectoid spaces with almost purity (P0–P6), BS22 perfectoidization through prisms (Q0–Q4, PR.0–PR.2) with crystalline, derived de Rham and enhanced derived-sheaf foundations, and the Kedlaya–Liu/Fargues–Scholze affinoid approximation. Tropical's extra theory (Berkovich spaces, skeleta, semistable reduction, intersection theory, tropical structure theorems) stacks on classical scheme foundations and is markedly shallower.

BorelRegulators needs all of higher algebraic K-theory (spectra, plus and Q-constructions, K₂ and K₃, scheme K-theory up to the motivic spectral sequence), adelic reduction theory with Borel–Serre, van Est and Borel's stable cohomology, Tate's thesis and the polylogarithm regulator. That is about twice the recorded theory of AdicEtaleGeometry, whose missing stack is adic spaces, perfectoid spaces with almost purity, prismatic perfectoidization and the étale and pro-étale sites.

Both rest on the same unbuilt K-theory foundation (spectra, plus/Q-constructions, K₂/K₃, finite generation with Borel–Serre). Borel adds stable cohomology of arithmetic groups, van Est, Tate's thesis, Borel's regulator theorem and the Beilinson comparison through higher Chow groups and the motivic spectral sequence (M.4, M.6), while EllipticK adds Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch (S.7), regular models of arithmetic surfaces, curve localisation and coniveau and, via its checkpoint, Tate's K₂ theorem with Poitou–Tate; the motivic spectral sequence and Borel's analytic theorems tip it.

EllipticK's missing theory is the K-theory tower with scheme K-theory, arithmetic surfaces and symbols. PadicHodgeTheory needs period rings and functors on perfectoid spaces, A_inf, crystalline and prismatic cohomology, diamonds and Fargues–Fontaine curves, the CohomologyComparisons theorems, p-adic monodromy, Breuil–Kisin/Fontaine–Laffaille, (φ,Γ)-modules and nearby cycles, a much larger and taller closure.

PadicHodgeTheory's closure already contains the étale duality and nearby-cycle theory that Weights uses (EDC.0–EDC.4, LPV.0–LPV.2, R34.3) and adds the whole p-adic stack (perfectoid spaces, A_inf, crystalline and prismatic cohomology, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves, CohomologyComparisons, (φ,Γ)-modules, p-adic monodromy). Weights' own extra theory is Deligne's Weil I/II and hard Lefschetz with Lefschetz-pencil monodromy (DWP, LPV.3–LPV.5).

Weights needs the unbuilt étale cohomology of schemes, duality and perverse sheaves (EDC), Lefschetz pencils and vanishing cycles (LPV) and Deligne's Weil I/II with hard Lefschetz (DWP). CohomologyComparisons needs a larger and taller p-adic tower (adic and perfectoid spaces, diamonds and Fargues–Fontaine curves, derived de Rham, full crystalline and prismatic cohomology, A_inf cohomology with BKF modules, period rings and sheaves) before its BMS and Česnavičius–Koshikawa comparisons.

NoncommutativeIwasawa needs completed group rings and Ore localization, K₁ localization and SK₁, Poitou–Tate with class field theory, Iwasawa complexes, Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-functions via Hilbert modular forms and the integral Brumer–Stark and Kurihara main conjecture before Kakde's theorem. CohomologyComparisons stacks more layers of foundational theory (enhanced derived sheaves, derived de Rham, crystalline, prismatic, perfectoid, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine, A_inf cohomology) beneath its comparisons; the amounts are close and the depth of the p-adic tower decides it.

Overconvergent forms sit on perfectoid Shimura varieties with Hodge–Tate period maps, canonical subgroups, integral Hilbert modular varieties and compactifications, automorphic bundles and the entire p-adic Hodge, A_inf, perfectoid and diamond stack. NoncommutativeIwasawa's missing Iwasawa-algebra, K-theory, Poitou–Tate and main-conjecture theory is large, but its closure is clearly smaller and lower.

OverconvergentAutomorphicForms imports CohomologyComparisons CP.0–CP.4 (through HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T1 and PadicHodgeTheory R06.5) together with nearly all of its p-adic stack. It adds Shimura data and varieties, toroidal and minimal compactifications, Hilbert modular integral models, perfectoid Shimura towers, locally analytic weight spaces and the BHW/AIP constructions.

Both need unbuilt K-theory: NoncommutativeIwasawa for relative K₁ localization and SK₁, Borel for the full plus/Q-construction, K₂/K₃, scheme K-theory and the motivic spectral sequence, and Borel also needs arithmetic groups, stable cohomology and Borel's regulator theorem. NoncommutativeIwasawa additionally needs Poitou–Tate with class field theory, Iwasawa cohomology, Kubota–Leopoldt and Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-functions over modular curves and Hilbert modular forms, integral Brumer–Stark and Kakde's congruences, a slightly larger closure.

Tropical's missing theory is nonarchimedean analytic geometry, semistable reduction, intersection theory and tropical/skeleton theory. Serre weights needs integral modular curves and stacks, Katz forms, finite flat group schemes with Breuil–Kisin modules and p-adic period rings, and Deligne's Galois representations resting on Weil II and local Langlands for GL₂, a far larger closure.

PadicHodgeTheory imports every stage AdicEtaleGeometry needs (A0–A4, perfectoid P0–P6, perfectoidization Q0–Q4 and their prismatic and crystalline foundations). It adds period rings and functors, A_inf and full crystalline cohomology, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves, CohomologyComparisons, p-adic monodromy, (φ,Γ)-modules and nearby cycles.

EllipticKTheory's missing theory is the K-theory tower, scheme K-theory with Riemann–Roch, arithmetic surfaces and symbols. OverconvergentAutomorphicForms needs Shimura varieties and compactifications, Hilbert modular integral models, perfectoid Shimura towers with Hodge–Tate period maps and the whole p-adic Hodge, A_inf and perfectoid stack, a much larger and taller closure.

StablePeriodicCurved's foundations largely exist (Mathlib triangulated categories and Verdier localization, Tau Ceti ExactStructure.IsFrobenius, MorphismIdeal quotients and DG algebras), leaving its own Happel, Buchweitz, Stai, Positselski and Orlov layers plus Cohen–Macaulay theory. ArithmeticStatistics needs several independent unbuilt theories: 2-covering and ring parametrizations, Davenport's lemma, uniformity sieves, p-adic Tamagawa masses and class field theory for class-group moments.

Weights needs étale cohomology of schemes, duality and perverse sheaves, Lefschetz pencils and Deligne's Weil I/II. NoncommutativeIwasawa needs Iwasawa algebras of p-adic Lie groups, K₁/SK₁ theory, Poitou–Tate with class field theory and Iwasawa complexes, Kubota–Leopoldt and Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-functions over modular curves and Hilbert modular forms, integral Brumer–Stark and Kakde's main conjecture, a broader closure of comparable depth.

Borel needs the K-theory tower up to higher Chow groups and the motivic spectral sequence, adelic reduction theory with Borel–Serre, stable cohomology and Borel's regulator theorem. CohomologyComparisons needs a larger and taller p-adic tower (adic and perfectoid spaces, diamonds, Fargues–Fontaine curves, derived de Rham, crystalline, prismatic and A_inf cohomology, period rings) before its comparison theorems.

Serre weights imports Weil I/II through R19.1 (Deligne's Galois representations), so most of Weights' closure lies inside its own. It adds integral modular curves with stacks and GAGA, Katz forms and theta operators, finite flat group schemes with Breuil–Kisin modules and p-adic period rings, and local Langlands for GL₂.

EllipticKTheory needs all of higher algebraic K-theory (spectra, plus and Q-constructions, K₂ and K₃), scheme K-theory with Riemann–Roch, finite generation with arithmetic-group reduction theory, and regular models of arithmetic surfaces. StablePeriodicCurved's homological algebra builds on existing Mathlib triangulated and derived categories and Tau Ceti exact structures, morphism ideals and DG algebras.

OverconvergentAutomorphicForms imports all of AdicEtaleGeometry (A0–A4 with its perfectoid and prismatic suppliers). It adds p-adic Hodge theory, A_inf and crystalline cohomology, diamonds, Shimura varieties and compactifications, perfectoid Shimura towers and the overconvergent coefficient constructions.
